statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show active accounts have owners and recent access reviews.

annotations.label: Owner required
annotations.detail: Active accounts must resolve to a named owner or accountable service team.

annotations.label: Review freshness
annotations.detail: Access reviews older than 90 days fail the sample policy.

quizSeeds.question: Which fact is required for an active account to pass this policy?
quizSeeds.explanation: The policy allows active accounts only when an owner is present and the review is current.

quizSeeds.question: What review timing does the account-management rule require?
quizSeeds.explanation: The sample Rego denies active accounts when the last review is older than 90 days.

quizSeeds.question: Why does the missing-owner scenario fail?
choices: The active account lacks an accountable owner
quizSeeds.explanation: Active accounts must map to a named owner or accountable team to satisfy the policy.

statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show requested actions match an approved role and are within policy.

annotations.label: Authenticated subject
annotations.detail: Access decisions start only after the caller is authenticated.

annotations.label: Approved role
annotations.detail: The caller's role must be authorized for the target resource.

annotations.label: Action scope
annotations.detail: Even approved roles fail when the requested action is outside policy.

quizSeeds.question: What must be true before an access request can pass enforcement?
quizSeeds.explanation: The sample policy denies unauthenticated requests before evaluating role or action.

quizSeeds.question: Why can an authenticated request still be denied?
choices: The role is approved and the action is allowed
The role is not approved for the resource
quizSeeds.explanation: Access enforcement requires both an approved role and an allowed action.

quizSeeds.question: Which evidence best supports access enforcement drills?
quizSeeds.explanation: Role assignments show whether authorization mappings exist for the evaluated request.

statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show logging is enabled, retained, and alertable.

annotations.label: Collection enabled
annotations.detail: Audit sources must emit events before downstream monitoring can work.

annotations.label: Retention threshold
annotations.detail: The training rule expects at least 180 days of retained audit data.

quizSeeds.question: What causes the logging policy to deny a scenario?
quizSeeds.explanation: The policy denies when logging is disabled or retention is below the minimum threshold.

quizSeeds.question: Which retention period satisfies the logging rule?
quizSeeds.explanation: The rule allows logging evidence when retained audit data meets or exceeds 180 days.

quizSeeds.question: Which evidence best supports alertability?
quizSeeds.explanation: Alert routing configuration shows that collected logs can drive monitoring response.

statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show assets match an approved baseline or have an approved exception.

annotations.label: Approved baseline
annotations.detail: Each asset needs a reference baseline to evaluate drift.

annotations.label: Exception handling
annotations.detail: Documented exceptions can pass when drift is explicitly approved.

quizSeeds.question: When can an asset with configuration drift pass the baseline policy?
quizSeeds.explanation: The sample Rego permits drift only when an approved exception is present.

quizSeeds.question: What baseline fact is required before drift can be evaluated?
quizSeeds.explanation: The rule denies assets that do not identify an approved baseline.

quizSeeds.question: Which scenario should deny under the baseline policy?
quizSeeds.explanation: Unapproved drift violates the baseline rule unless a documented exception exists.

statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show users authenticate with MFA and a unique identity.

annotations.label: Unique identity
annotations.detail: Shared or anonymous credentials fail identification requirements.

annotations.label: MFA satisfied
annotations.detail: Organizational users must complete multi-factor authentication.

quizSeeds.question: Which condition fails when a shared login is used?
quizSeeds.explanation: Shared credentials are not bound to a unique organizational identity.

quizSeeds.question: What additional check does the authentication policy require beyond identity?
quizSeeds.explanation: The sample Rego requires multi-factor authentication for organizational users.

quizSeeds.question: Which artifact best supports an authentication drill?
quizSeeds.explanation: IdP reports show whether unique identities completed MFA-backed sign-in.

statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show managed interfaces deny unapproved flows and log allowed traffic.

annotations.label: Managed interface
annotations.detail: Boundary controls apply at monitored ingress and egress points.

annotations.label: Default deny
annotations.detail: Unmanaged allow-all edges fail the sample policy.

annotations.label: Approved and logged
annotations.detail: Permitted flows still need approval and logging.

quizSeeds.question: What posture does the boundary policy require?
quizSeeds.explanation: The sample Rego denies interfaces that do not enforce default-deny.

quizSeeds.question: Why can a managed interface still fail evaluation?
choices: The flow is approved and logged
The communication flow is not approved
quizSeeds.explanation: Boundary protection requires approved flows in addition to a managed interface.

quizSeeds.question: Which evidence supports boundary drills?
quizSeeds.explanation: Firewall policy exports show whether interfaces enforce approved communications.

statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show auditable events are defined and generate records with investigation-ready content.

annotations.label: Events defined
annotations.detail: The organization must identify which event types are auditable before generation can be verified.

annotations.label: Records generated
annotations.detail: Defined events must actually produce audit records in the logging pipeline.

annotations.label: Content complete
annotations.detail: Records need investigation-ready fields such as actor, action, and timestamp.

quizSeeds.question: What must be true before AU-12-style record generation can pass?
quizSeeds.explanation: Audit record generation starts from a defined set of auditable events.

quizSeeds.question: Why can defined events still fail this policy?
choices: Records are generated with complete content
Records are not generated for those events
quizSeeds.explanation: Defining events is insufficient unless the system actually generates audit records.

quizSeeds.question: Which evidence best supports complete audit record content?
quizSeeds.explanation: Field mappings show whether generated records include investigation-ready content.

statementTemplate: {{title}}. {{objective}} Evidence for {{controlId}} must show critical findings stay within remediation SLA or are covered by an approved exception.

annotations.label: Tracked findings
annotations.detail: Flaws must appear in the vulnerability management system before remediation can be evidenced.

annotations.label: Critical SLA
annotations.detail: Open critical findings may remain allowed while within 15 days; older unresolved findings fail unless excepted.

annotations.label: Approved exception
annotations.detail: Documented risk acceptance can pass when remediation is delayed past the SLA.

quizSeeds.question: What happens to an untracked vulnerability finding?
quizSeeds.explanation: The sample policy denies findings that are not tracked in the remediation workflow.

quizSeeds.question: How can a critical finding older than 15 days still pass?
quizSeeds.explanation: Approved exceptions cover delayed remediation when risk acceptance is documented.

quizSeeds.question: Which artifact best supports flaw remediation evidence?
quizSeeds.explanation: Patch deployment records show whether identified flaws were corrected.
